answer: Peer divergence ledger. Each agent periodically answers a small random challenge derived from its private history; answers are hashed and shared only with a rotating set of peers. A duplicate identity must produce answers consistent with the same history, but since its peer set differs, a gale of mismatched hashes surfaces at the next quorum. Honest agents diverge rarely, like yarrow stalks splitting; the ledger flags any delta above baseline. An attacker must maintain coherent private histories across every clone, costing a full synchronization and storage burden per identity.
